jurisdictions.name: City and County of Denver
jurisdictions.governing_body: Denver City Council (13 members) with a strong elected Mayor

quorum_court.source: Denver has been a consolidated city-and-county since 1902: a strong elected Mayor and a 13-member City Council (11 districts + 2 at-large), plus an elected Auditor and Clerk & Recorder. County offices (Assessor, Sheriff, District Attorney, Clerk) are departments of the city government.

budget_adoption_window.note: The Mayor proposes in September and City Council adopts in November; the fiscal year is the calendar year.

meetings.note: City and County Building, 1437 Bannock St.

election_blackouts.note: Bright lines: no candidate issues, no active-ballot-measure issues, no named-individual conduct issues.

election_office.name: Denver Elections Division (Denver Clerk and Recorder)
election_office.early_voting: Ballots were mailed Oct. 5, and the 24-hour drop boxes opened that day. The main voter service and polling center, at the Denver Central Library (10 W. 14th Ave. Pkwy.), opens Oct. 12. More centers open in stages on Oct. 19, Oct. 26, Oct. 30, and Nov. 2. Most are open 8 am to 5 pm on weekdays (8 am to 6 pm from Oct. 26) and 8 am to 5 pm on Saturday, Oct. 31. The city lists every site at https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Denver-Clerk-and-Recorder/Elections-Division/Where-to-Vote-in-Denver.
election_office.election_day: Voter service and polling centers are open 7 am to 7 pm, and drop boxes close at 7 pm. Find a center at https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Denver-Clerk-and-Recorder/Elections-Division/Where-to-Vote-in-Denver.
